To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the postnatal recruitment of UCP3 expression is impaired in the skeletal muscle in very preterm newborn infants and 2) AMPK may be involved in control of both the expression of UCP3 and of GLUT4 in skeletal muscle of preterm neonates.
the expression of the genes for mitochondrial uncoupler UCP3 and glucose transporter GLUT4 is impaired in preterm newborn skeletal muscle.
the expression of UCP3 and the glucose transporter GLUT4 in the skeletal muscle is controlled by AMPK in the neonate and that this control is defective in the very preterm newborn.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the switch between glycolysis and fatty acid oxidation in the skeletal muscle during the postnatal period.
the mechanism for delayed postnatal recruitment of metabolic genes in the skeletal muscle.

the delayed development of the metabolic switch in the skeletal muscles of preterm newborns, a phenomenon that might be linked to a defect in the control of gene expression by nutritional factors and AMPK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the defect in the postnatal expression of UCP3 is not related to the impaired expression of the GLUT4 gene.

the postnatal switch from glycolysis to oxidative metabolism in the skeletal muscle is impaired in very preterm newborn babies, and that the defect is caused by the delayed postnatal recruitment of both genes, UCP and GLUT4, by lipids.
the postnatal switch between oxidative and glycolytic metabolism is delayed in the skeletal muscles of very immature newborns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the delayed postnatal recruitment of genes for UCP3 and glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) in preterm neonates is linked with impaired AMPK activation and may be a cause for their delayed development of skeletal muscle energy metabolism.
the postnatal switch in skeletal muscles of preterm neonates is delayed by a defect in the control of the UCP-3 gene by AMPK.

AMPK, in concert with the transcription factor peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma (PPAR-gamma), may play an essential role in the control of the expression of UCP3 and the glucose transporter GLUT4 in skeletal muscle of the neonates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMPK-UCP3-GLUT4 pathway is impaired in the skeletal muscle in very preterm newborn.
UCP3 gene is regulated by AMP-activated protein kinases and that the defect in the control of the UCP gene by nutritional lipids is involved in delayed postnatal development of energy metabolism.
AMPK is a possible mediator of the delayed postnatal recruitment of UCP3 and the switch from glycolytic to oxidative metabolism.
